(896,
 '# IMPLEMENTATION PLAN — ai-loop v4.6 Startup Policy Deferral, Hydration-Safe Hard Gate & Live Full-Loop Convergence

**Generated:** 2026-09-22T23:57-05:00  
**Current runtime family:** ai-loop v4.x  
**Target release:** ai-loop `v4.6.0`  
**Execution environment:** Ubuntu / WSL control plane  
**Controller:** `/opt/ai-loop/ai-loopd-v3.py`  
**Browser broker:** `/opt/ai-loop/browser-broker-v1.cjs`  
**Target project:** `bot_trading`  
**Target branch:** `feature/GRU`  
**Observed failing run:** `R20260922T160843`  

---

# 0. Mandatory objective

The implementation is complete only when a real Ubuntu live canary executes the entire loop successfully and ends at independently validated:

```text
FINAL_GO
AI_LOOP_COMPLETE=GO
```

The implementation team MUST NOT stop after fixing the current startup policy bug.

If any new bug appears during unit, integration, restart, synthetic, or live testing, the team must:

```text
capture evidence
→ reproduce deterministically
→ add regression test
→ fix root cause
→ rerun complete test suite
→ rerun 100-loop synthetic soak
→ rerun a brand-new live canary
→ repeat until FINAL_GO
```

An ai-loop implementation defect is never an acceptable final blocker.

---

# 1. Current diagnosis

The last real run produced:

```text
ai-loopd-v3 version=4.4.0 run=R20260922T160843 phase=IMPLEMENTING
OPENCODE_SEMANTIC_CAPABILITY=PASS
BROWSER_BROKER=PASS
DETERMINISTIC_CHAT_POLICY RETRY attempt=1 purpose=startup
  CHAT_SURFACE_HYDRATION_TIMEOUT
DETERMINISTIC_CHAT_POLICY RETRY attempt=2 purpose=startup
  CHAT_SURFACE_HYDRATION_TIMEOUT
CHATGPT_CHAT_POLICY_GUARD_FAILED
```

The controller exited before doing useful reconciliation.

The current failure class has two distinct root causes.

## 1.1 Hydration ordering bug

The browser policy logic can treat the presence of the reasoning trigger (`High`) as enough evidence that policy controls are hydrated.

Conceptually:

```javascript
return q.chat || q.trigger ? q : null;
```

This is unsafe because the reasoning trigger may mount before the Chat/Work surface control.

Possible live sequence:

```text
t=0 ms     High trigger exists
           Chat control absent

t=300 ms   High trigger exists
           Chat control absent

t=900 ms   High trigger exists
           Chat control appears and is selected
```

The current implementation may stop waiting at `t=0` because `q.trigger` is truthy.

It then tries to interact with Chat before Chat exists.

## 1.2 Truthy-object wait predicate bug

A wait such as:

```javascript
waitUntil(() => observe('surface_actionable'))
```

is unsafe if `observe()` always returns an object.

The object itself is truthy even when:

```text
surface_actionable = false
```

The wait can therefore finish immediately.

Every wait predicate must return either:

```text
true / valid terminal state
```

or:

```text
false / null
```

until its actual condition is satisfied.

## 1.3 Startup policy guard is placed too early

The runtime currently treats startup policy verification as a fatal gate.

That is unnecessary during a resume/startup phase when the controller is only trying to:

- observe current state;
- reconcile an existing run;
- read an existing conversation;
- decide what phase it is in.

There is no outbound side effect yet.

The hard Chat/Sol/High gate belongs immediately before any outbound controller message.

Correct architecture:

```text
startup / resume
    ↓
browser starts
    ↓
best-effort startup policy probe
    ├─ PASS → checkpoint
    └─ temporarily unproven → log + continue read-only
    ↓
reconcile state
    ↓
observe assistant / CI / pending actions
    ↓
before ANY outbound Send
    ↓
HARD POLICY GATE
    ↓
Chat + GPT-5.6 Sol + High proven
    ↓
Send allowed
```

---

# 2. Non-negotiable invariants

1. `startup` / `resume` policy failure caused only by temporary UI hydration MUST NOT terminate the controller.
2. Startup must never send a message while policy is unproven.
3. Every outbound Send MUST execute a fresh hard policy gate.
4. The hard policy gate must prove:
   ```text
   surface = Chat
   model contract = GPT-5.6 Sol
   reasoning = High
   ```
5. The reasoning trigger MUST NOT satisfy the Chat surface hydration wait.
6. A truthy object MUST NOT accidentally satisfy a wait predicate.
7. No blind resend after possible Send.
8. No duplicate attachment/action/commit/pipeline side effect after restart.
9. Startup deferral must not weaken final pre-Send safety.
10. The implementation team must continue live debugging until a full loop reaches validated GO.

---

# 3. Target architecture

## 3.1 Startup policy probe

Introduce explicit modes:

```text
POLICY_PROBE
POLICY_HARD_GATE
```

### `POLICY_PROBE`

Used at:

```text
startup
resume
read-only reconciliation
```

Behavior:

```text
try to observe Chat/Sol/High
if PASS:
    persist policy checkpoint
if temporarily unavailable:
    persist DEFERRED
    preserve diagnostics
    continue read-only
if definitely wrong but correctable:
    optional bounded correction is allowed
if unsafe/unknown:
    do not Send
    continue only read-only paths
```

A probe must not cause process termination merely because the UI is not hydrated.

### `POLICY_HARD_GATE`

Used immediately before:

```text
bootstrap Send
evidence Send
procede
follow-up
final-review request
diagnosis request
replan request
any other controller-originated message
```

Behavior:

```text
wait until Chat surface controls are actually hydrated
prove Chat selected
wait until reasoning/model control is hydrated
prove High
prove Sol contract
only then permit Send
```

A hard gate failure blocks Send but should leave the controller alive when safe to retry later.

---

# 4. Surface hydration state machine

Implement explicit states:

```text
SURFACE_UNKNOWN
SURFACE_WAITING
SURFACE_CHAT_SELECTED
SURFACE_WORK_SELECTED
SURFACE_OTHER_SELECTED
SURFACE_TIMEOUT
```

## 4.1 Surface wait predicate

Correct predicate shape:

```javascript
const q = await observeSurface();

if (q.chatSelected) return q;
if (q.chatActionable) return q;
if (q.otherSurfaceSelected && q.chatActionable) return q;

return null;
```

Do NOT use:

```javascript
return q;
```

Do NOT use reasoning state as a substitute for surface readiness.

## 4.2 Reasoning wait

Only after the surface phase is complete:

```text
surface == Chat
```

begin the reasoning phase.

Correct reasoning predicate:

```javascript
const q = await observeReasoning();

if (q.selectedEffort === 'high') return q;
if (q.reasoningControlActionable) return q;

return null;
```

---

# 5. Hard policy gate

The final proof immediately before Send must be performed in one deterministic broker operation.

Required proof:

```json
{
  "surface": "chat",
  "surface_selected": true,
  "reasoning": "high",
  "model_contract": "gpt-5.6-sol",
  "proof": {
    "surface": "...",
    "reasoning": "...",
    "model": "..."
  }
}
```

If any field is UNKNOWN:

```text
SEND FORBIDDEN
```

---

# 6. Startup/resume behavior

Current behavior:

```text
ensure_chat_policy(startup)
→ error
→ raise RuntimeError
→ daemon exits
```

Target:

```text
startup_policy_probe()
    ↓
PASS
or
DEFERRED_TRANSIENT
    ↓
persist checkpoint
    ↓
continue FSM read-only reconciliation
```

Example desired log:

```text
STARTUP_POLICY PROBE_DEFERRED reason=CHAT_SURFACE_NOT_HYDRATED
STARTUP_POLICY controller_continues_read_only=true
```

Later, before a Send:

```text
OUTBOUND_POLICY HARD_GATE purpose=evidence_send
CHAT_SURFACE PASS surface=chat
MODEL_GUARD PASS model=gpt-5.6-sol reasoning=high
DELIVERY_READY ...
```

---

# 7. Controller changes

The controller must classify policy errors.

## 7.1 Retryable/deferred

Examples:

```text
CHAT_SURFACE_HYDRATION_TIMEOUT
REASONING_CONTROL_HYDRATION_TIMEOUT
SURFACE_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE
BROWSER_UI_NOT_SETTLED
```

At startup/resume:

```text
defer + continue read-only
```

Before Send:

```text
block Send + bounded retry/poll
```

## 7.2 Fatal policy errors

Examples:

```text
WRONG_ACCOUNT
PROJECT_CONTEXT_OTHER
UNSAFE_SURFACE
UNRECOVERABLE_BROWSER_AUTH
```

These may stop outbound work and require explicit resolution.

They must not be conflated with hydration delay.

---

# 8. Team

**Team size: 8**

| Role | Code | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Technical Lead | TL | integration, invariants, release decision |
| Browser Policy Engineer | BPE | hydration and Chat/Sol/High broker logic |
| Controller/FSM Engineer | CFE | startup deferral, pre-Send hard gate |

| Test & Chaos Engineer | TCE | regressions, fault injection, soak |
| SRE / Live Validation Engineer | SRE | Ubuntu canary, diagnostics, repeated live cycles |
| Independent Auditor | IRA | evidence review and release gates |

q : null;\n```\n\nThis is unsafe because the reasoning trigger may mount before the Chat/Work surface control.\n\nPossible live sequence:\n\n```text\nt=0 ms     High trigger exists\n           Chat control absent\n\nt=300 ms   High trigger exists\n           Chat control absent\n\nt=900 ms   High trigger exists\n           Chat control appears and is selected\n```\n\nThe current implementation may stop waiting at `t=0` because `q.trigger` is truthy.\n\nIt then tries to interact with Chat before Chat exists.\n\n## 1.2 Truthy-object wait predicate bug\n\nA wait such as:\n\n```javascript\nwaitUntil(() => observe(\'surface_actionable\'))\n```\n\nis unsafe if `observe()` always returns an object.\n\nThe object itself is truthy even when:\n\n```text\nsurface_actionable = false\n```\n\nThe wait can therefore finish immediately.\n\nEvery wait predicate must return either:\n\n```text\ntrue / valid terminal state\n```\n\nor:\n\n```text\nfalse / null\n```\n\nuntil its actual condition is satisfied.\n\n## 1.3 Startup policy guard is placed too early\n\nThe runtime currently treats startup policy verification as a fatal gate.\n\nThat is unnecessary during a resume/startup phase when the controller is only trying to:\n\n- observe current state;\n- reconcile an existing run;\n- read an existing conversation;\n- decide what phase it is in.\n\nThere is no outbound side effect yet.\n\nThe hard Chat/Sol/High gate belongs immediately before any outbound controller message.\n\nCorrect architecture:\n\n```text\nstartup / resume\n    ↓\nbrowser starts\n    ↓\nbest-effort startup policy probe\n    ├─ PASS → checkpoint\n    └─ temporarily unproven → log + continue read-only\n    ↓\nreconcile state\n    ↓\nobserve assistant / CI / pending actions\n    ↓\nbefore ANY outbound Send\n    ↓\nHARD POLICY GATE\n    ↓\nChat + GPT-5.6 Sol + High proven\n    ↓\nSend allowed\n```\n\n---\n\n# 2. Non-negotiable invariants\n\n1. `startup` / `resume` policy failure caused only by temporary UI hydration MUST NOT terminate the controller.\n2. Startup must never send a message while policy is unproven.\n3. Every outbound Send MUST execute a fresh hard policy gate.\n4. The hard policy gate must prove:\n   ```text\n   surface = Chat\n   model contract = GPT-5.6 Sol\n   reasoning = High\n   ```\n5. The reasoning trigger MUST NOT satisfy the Chat surface hydration wait.\n6. A truthy object MUST NOT accidentally satisfy a wait predicate.\n7. No blind resend after possible Send.\n8. No duplicate attachment/action/commit/pipeline side effect after restart.\n9. Startup deferral must not weaken final pre-Send safety.\n10. The implementation team must continue live debugging until a full loop reaches validated GO.\n\n---\n\n# 3. Target architecture\n\n## 3.1 Startup policy probe\n\nIntroduce explicit modes:\n\n```text\nPOLICY_PROBE\nPOLICY_HARD_GATE\n```\n\n### `POLICY_PROBE`\n\nUsed at:\n\n```text\nstartup\nresume\nread-only reconciliation\n```\n\nBehavior:\n\n```text\ntry to observe Chat/Sol/High\nif PASS:\n    persist policy checkpoint\nif temporarily unavailable:\n    persist DEFERRED\n    preserve diagnostics\n    continue read-only\nif definitely wrong but correctable:\n    optional bounded correction is allowed\nif unsafe/unknown:\n    do not Send\n    continue only read-only paths\n```\n\nA probe must not cause process termination merely because the UI is not hydrated.\n\n### `POLICY_HARD_GATE`\n\nUsed immediately before:\n\n```text\nbootstrap Send\nevidence Send\nprocede\nfollow-up\nfinal-review request\ndiagnosis request\nreplan request\nany other controller-originated message\n```\n\nBehavior:\n\n```text\nwait until Chat surface controls are actually hydrated\nprove Chat selected\nwait until reasoning/model control is hydrated\nprove High\nprove Sol contract\nonly then permit Send\n```\n\nA hard gate failure blocks Send but should leave the controller alive when safe to retry later.\n\n---\n\n# 4. Surface hydration state machine\n\nImplement explicit states:\n\n```text\nSURFACE_UNKNOWN\nSURFACE_WAITING\nSURFACE_CHAT_SELECTED\nSURFACE_WORK_SELECTED\nSURFACE_OTHER_SELECTED\nSURFACE_TIMEOUT\n```\n\n## 4.1 Surface wait predicate\n\nCorrect predicate shape:\n\n```javascript\nconst q = await observeSurface();\n\nif (q.chatSelected) return q;\nif (q.chatActionable) return q;\nif (q.otherSurfaceSelected && q.chatActionable) return q;\n\nreturn null;\n```\n\nDo NOT use:\n\n```javascript\nreturn q;\n```\n\nDo NOT use reasoning state as a substitute for surface readiness.\n\n## 4.2 Reasoning wait\n\nOnly after the surface phase is complete:\n\n```text\nsurface == Chat\n```\n\nbegin the reasoning phase.\n\nCorrect reasoning predicate:\n\n```javascript\nconst q = await observeReasoning();\n\nif (q.selectedEffort === \'high\') return q;\nif (q.reasoningControlActionable) return q;\n\nreturn null;\n```\n\n---\n\n# 5. Hard policy gate\n\nThe final proof immediately before Send must be performed in one deterministic broker operation.\n\nRequired proof:\n\n```json\n{\n  "surface": "chat",\n  "surface_selected": true,\n  "reasoning": "high",\n  "model_contract": "gpt-5.6-sol",\n  "proof": {\n    "surface": "...",\n    "reasoning": "...",\n    "model": "..."\n  }\n}\n```\n\nIf any field is UNKNOWN:\n\n```text\nSEND FORBIDDEN\n```\n\n---\n\n# 6. Startup/resume behavior\n\nCurrent behavior:\n\n```text\nensure_chat_policy(startup)\n→ error\n→ raise RuntimeError\n→ daemon exits\n```\n\nTarget:\n\n```text\nstartup_policy_probe()\n    ↓\nPASS\nor\nDEFERRED_TRANSIENT\n    ↓\npersist checkpoint\n    ↓\ncontinue FSM read-only reconciliation\n```\n\nExample desired log:\n\n```text\nSTARTUP_POLICY PROBE_DEFERRED reason=CHAT_SURFACE_NOT_HYDRATED\nSTARTUP_POLICY controller_continues_read_only=true\n```\n\nLater, before a Send:\n\n```text\nOUTBOUND_POLICY HARD_GATE purpose=evidence_send\nCHAT_SURFACE PASS surface=chat\nMODEL_GUARD PASS model=gpt-5.6-sol reasoning=high\nDELIVERY_READY ...\n```\n\n---\n\n# 7. Controller changes\n\nThe controller must classify policy errors.\n\n## 7.1 Retryable/deferred\n\nExamples:\n\n```text\nCHAT_SURFACE_HYDRATION_TIMEOUT\nREASONING_CONTROL_HYDRATION_TIMEOUT\nSURFACE_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE\nBROWSER_UI_NOT_SETTLED\n```\n\nAt startup/resume:\n\n```text\ndefer + continue read-only\n```\n\nBefore Send:\n\n```text\nblock Send + bounded retry/poll\n```\n\n## 7.2 Fatal policy errors\n\nExamples:\n\n```text\nWRONG_ACCOUNT\nPROJECT_CONTEXT_OTHER\nUNSAFE_SURFACE\nUNRECOVERABLE_BROWSER_AUTH\n```\n\nThese may stop outbound work and require explicit resolution.\n\nThey must not be conflated with hydration delay.\n\n---\n\n# 8. 790: # 13. Pre-mortem
791: 
792: ## Failure 1 — startup deferral accidentally weakens Send safety
793: 
794: **Mitigation**
795: - one central outbound Send function;
796: - hard policy gate inside that function;
797: - source-wide audit;
798: - test that every outbound message passes through it.
799: 
800: ## Failure 2 — hydration bug moves from Chat surface to reasoning control
801: 
802: **Mitigation**
803: - independent surface and reasoning state machines;
804: - explicit condition predicates;
805: - delayed-control fixtures.
806: 
807: ## Failure 3 — controller remains alive but spins forever
808: 
809: **Mitigation**
810: - bounded read-only reconciliation intervals;
811: - phase progress watchdog;
812: - structured diagnostics;
813: - no blind high-frequency polling.
814: 
815: ## Failure 4 — later live stage exposes new untested bug
816: 
817: **Mitigation**
818: - mandatory recursive fix-until-GO protocol;
819: - team cannot stop at first downstream failure.
820: 
821: ---
822: 
823: # 14. ADR
824: 
825: ## Decision
826: 
827: Make startup policy verification non-fatal for transient hydration failures, while making the pre-Send policy gate stronger and centralized.
828: 
829: ## Why
830: 
831: Startup/read-only reconciliation has no outbound side effect and therefore does not need to die because a visual control has not mounted yet.
832: 
833: Outbound Send is the safety boundary.
834: 
835: ## Consequences
836: 
837: Positive:
838: 
839: - resume is resilient to transient UI hydration;
840: - no weaker Send protection;
841: - fewer unnecessary daemon restarts;
842: - clearer separation between read-only reconciliation and side effects.
843: 
844: Costs:
845: 
846: - controller policy state becomes two-mode;
847: - requires comprehensive outbound-message audit.

384: 
385: The controller must classify policy errors.

393: REASONING_CONTROL_HYDRATION_TIMEOUT
394: SURFACE_TEMPORARILY_UNAVAILABLE
395: BROWSER_UI_NOT_SETTLED

399: 
400: ```text
401: defer + continue read-only
402: ```
403: 
404: Before Send:
405: 
406: ```text
407: block Send + bounded retry/poll

416: PROJECT_CONTEXT_OTHER

pt-0 pb-3 md:px-5 InlineCodePane-EYx4bd" dir="ltr"><code class="whitespace-pre! block text-size-code CodeContent-ybJ8Tl"><span>set -Eeuo pipefail
umask 077

SHA="0c11a13e0c6ceb4c9eab3258ce4a10728fcb6390"
BRANCH="feature/GRU"
SEM_WF="0f6fcfa4-4fb0-419d-ba4d-ca77af5d0c62"
SEM_PPL="4df05bd2-6a81-41dc-9dfe-9e0051cd602c"

E="/tmp/ai-loop-sem-readonly-${SHA:0:12}-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
mkdir -p "$E"

fail() {
  echo "READONLY_EVIDENCE=FAILED"
  echo "BLOCKER=$1"
  echo "EVIDENCE_DIR=$E"
  exit "${2:-90}"
}

for c in curl jq grep tail sha256sum; do
  command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail "MISSING_COMMAND:$c" 91
done

if [ -f /opt/ai-loop/ai-loop.env ]; then
  set -a
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source /opt/ai-loop/ai-loop.env
  set +a
fi

SEM_TOKEN="${SEMAPHORE_API_TOKEN:-${SEMAPHORE_TOKEN:-}}"
SEM_BASE="${SEMAPHORE_API_URL:-${SEMAPHORE_ORG_URL:-${SEMAPHORE_URL:-${SEMAPHORE_SERVER_URL:-}}}}"

[ -n "$SEM_TOKEN" ] || fail "SEMAPHORE_TOKEN_NOT_AVAILABLE" 92
[ -n "$SEM_BASE" ] || fail "SEMAPHORE_BASE_URL_NOT_AVAILABLE" 93

SEM_BASE="${SEM_BASE%/}"
case "$SEM_BASE" in
  */api/v1alpha) SEM_API="$SEM_BASE" ;;
  *) SEM_API="$SEM_BASE/api/v1alpha" ;;
esac

curl -fsSL \
  -H "Authorization: Token $SEM_TOKEN" \
  -H "User-Agent: ai-loop-readonly-evidence" \
  "$SEM_API/plumber-workflows/$SEM_WF" \
  > "$E/workflow.json" \
  || fail "WORKFLOW_FETCH_FAILED" 101

curl -fsSL \
  -H "Authorization: Token $SEM_TOKEN" \
  -H "User-Agent: ai-loop-readonly-evidence" \
  "$SEM_API/pipelines/$SEM_PPL?detailed=true" \
  > "$E/pipeline.json" \
  || fail "PIPELINE_FETCH_FAILED" 102

WF_ID="$(jq -r '(.workflow // .).wf_id // empty' "$E/workflow.json")"
WF_SHA="$(jq -r '(.workflow // .).commit_sha // empty' "$E/workflow.json")"
WF_BRANCH="$(jq -r '(.workflow // .).branch_name // empty' "$E/workflow.json")"

PPL_ID="$(jq -r '(.pipeline // .).ppl_id // empty' "$E/pipeline.json")"
PPL_WF="$(jq -r '(.pipeline // .).wf_id // empty' "$E/pipeline.json")"

[ "$WF_ID" = "$SEM_WF" ] || fail "WORKFLOW_ID_MISMATCH:$WF_ID" 111
[ "$WF_SHA" = "$SHA" ] || fail "WORKFLOW_SHA_MISMATCH:$WF_SHA" 112
[ "$WF_BRANCH" = "$BRANCH" ] || fail "WORKFLOW_BRANCH_MISMATCH:$WF_BRANCH" 113
[ "$PPL_ID" = "$SEM_PPL" ] || fail "PIPELINE_ID_MISMATCH:$PPL_ID" 114
[ "$PPL_WF" = "$SEM_WF" ] || fail "PIPELINE_WORKFLOW_MISMATCH:$PPL_WF" 115

echo "===== EXACT IDENTITY ====="
jq '(.workflow // .) | {
  wf_id, commit_sha, branch_name, created_at, rerun_of
}' "$E/workflow.json"

jq '(.pipeline // .) | {
  ppl_id, wf_id, name, state, result, result_reason,
  error_description, branch_name, yaml_file_name,
  created_at, running_at, done_at
}' "$E/pipeline.json"

jq -r '
  (.blocks // [])[] as $b |
  ($b.jobs // [])[] |
  [
    ($b.name // ""),
    (.name // ""),
    (.job_id // .id // ""),
    (.status // .state // ""),
    (.result // "")
  ] | @tsv
' "$E/pipeline.json" > "$E/jobs.tsv"

echo "===== ALL JOBS ====="
cat "$E/jobs.tsv"

mkdir -p "$E/jobs"
: > "$E/non-success-summary.txt"

while IFS=$'\t' read -r block job jid status result; do
  [ -n "$jid" ] || continue

  curl -fsSL \
    -H "Authorization: Token $SEM_TOKEN" \
    -H "User-Agent: ai-loop-readonly-evidence" \
    "$SEM_API/jobs/$jid" \
    > "$E/jobs/$jid.metadata.json" || true

  http="$(
    curl -sSL \
      -o "$E/jobs/$jid.log.raw" \
      -w '%{http_code}' \
      -H "Authorization: Token $SEM_TOKEN" \
      -H "User-Agent: ai-loop-readonly-evidence" \
      "$SEM_API/logs/$jid"
  )"

  case "${result,,}:${status,,}" in
    *failed*|*failure*|*stopped*|*cancelled*|*canceled*|*error*)
      {
        echo "============================================================"
        echo "BLOCK=$block"
        echo "JOB=$job"
        echo "JOB_ID=$jid"
        echo "STATUS=$status"
        echo "RESULT=$result"
        echo "LOG_HTTP=$http"

        if [[ "$http" =~ ^2 ]] && jq -e . "$E/jobs/$jid.log.raw" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "--- NONZERO DIRECTIVES ---"
          jq -r '
            [
              ..
              | objects
              | select(
                  .exit_code? != null
                  and (((.exit_code|tonumber?) // 0) != 0)
                )
              | {
                  directive:(.directive // .command // .name // "UNKNOWN"),
                  exit_code,
                  started_at,
                  finished_at,
                  output:(.output // .message // .text // null)
                }
            ]
          ' "$E/jobs/$jid.log.raw"

          echo "--- LOG TAIL ---"
          tail -c 20000 "$E/jobs/$jid.log.raw"
          echo
        elif [[ "$http" =~ ^2 ]]; then
          echo "--- FAILURE LINES ---"
          grep -nEi \
            'exit code|exited with|command failed|failed|error:|fatal:|permission denied|timed out|timeout|not found|denied|stopped|cancel' \
            "$E/jobs/$jid.log.raw" | head -250 || true
          echo "--- LOG TAIL ---"
          tail -c 20000 "$E/jobs/$jid.log.raw"
          echo
        else
          echo "LOG_UNAVAILABLE_HTTP=$http"
        fi
      } >> "$E/non-success-summary.txt"
      ;;
  esac
done < "$E/jobs.tsv"

echo "===== NON-SUCCESS JOB EVIDENCE ====="
cat "$E/non-success-summary.txt"

echo "===== EVIDENCE DIGEST ====="
sha256sum "$E/workflow.json" "$E/pipeline.json" "$E/jobs.tsv" "$E/non-success-summary.txt"

echo "SEMAPHORE_RERUN=NO"
echo "SEMAPHORE_RETRY=NO"
echo "SEMAPHORE_MUTATION=NO"
echo "REPOSITORY_MUTATION=NO"
echo "VPS_MUTATION=NO"
echo "EVIDENCE_DIR=$E"
echo "READONLY_EVIDENCE=PASS"</span></code></div></div></div><p class="Paragraph-kKnbIo" dir="auto"><span>No se debe crear otro commit: </span><span data-markdown-copy="inline-code" class="inline-markdown InlineMarkdownIsolate-QWDV4W" dir="ltr">0c11a13e…</span><span> ya es el HEAD remoto y corresponde al commit v4.6 existente. El siguiente paso depende únicamente del resultado de esta acción; con </span><span data-markdown-copy="inline-code" class="inline-markdown InlineMarkdownIsolate-QWDV4W" dir="ltr">block/job/directive/exit_code</span><span> podremos distinguir un defecto real de v4.6 de un fallo de infraestructura o una detención externa, sin gastar otro run de Keep turns short, concrete, and tied to real work.\n\n## Required Flow\n\nFollow this order:\n\n1. Role selection, only if launch context does not already supply roles\n2. First-task selection\n3. Context-source selection\n4. Context retrieval and candidate discovery\n5. Task-anchor selection or discovery\n6. Substance pass over retrieved context\n7. Do not reopen a completed step.\n\n## Non-Negotiables\n\n- Use `setup_codex_step` for each setup step that is still needed.\n- Launch-context roles are authoritative. Start Codex setup\n2. Personalize Codex\n3. Choose a first task\n4. Give Codex context\n5. Get something done\n\nKeep the labels exact. Keep at most one step `in_progress`.\n\nMark steps complete only when their real work is complete:\n\n- `Start Codex setup`: Setup Codex skill invocation received\n- `Personalize Codex`: role selected or supplied by launch context\n- `Choose a first task`: task selected\n- `Give Codex context`: usable context was retrieved, context was explicitly skipped, or unavailable context was recovered\n- `Get something done`: artifact or allowed starter template was created\n\n## Surfaces\n\nUse the most native available surface:\n\n1. `setup_codex_step` with `step: \"role\"` only when launch context does not supply roles\n2. `setup_codex_step` with `step: \"task\"` for first-task selection\n3. `setup_codex_step` with `step: \"context\"` for context selection\n4. `request_onboarding_input` for onboarding choice questions\n5. `request_option_picker` for compact non-onboarding choices\n6. Connector modals for authorization\n7. `setup_codex_step` with `step: \"complete\"` after the artifact is created\n\nThe `role`, `task`, and `context` setup steps return inline. Continue after they return. For `request_onboarding_input` and `request_option_picker`, stop immediately after calling the tool.\n\nIf any setup step returns `action: \"dismiss\"`, stop onboarding. Treat `action: \"skip\"` as a choice to continue with documented defaults.\n\n## Step 1 - Role\n\nFirst inspect launch context.\n\nIf launch context supplies selected roles:\n\n- Treat those roles as authoritative.\n- Mark `Personalize Codex` complete.\n- Do not ask the user to confirm the roles.\n- Do not call `setup_codex_step` with `step: \"role\"`.\n- Briefly acknowledge the supplied roles.\n- Proceed directly to Step 2 and call `setup_codex_step` with `step: \"task\"`.\n\nOnly when launch context does not supply roles, say:\n\n\u003e Hi {name}, welcome to Codex. You can hand off real work here: reading context, writing docs, searching across tools, checking changes, and following up.\n\u003e\n\u003e Let's get you set up. To start, what type of work do you do?\n\nThen call `setup_codex_step` with `step: \"role\"`.\n\n## Role Defaults\n\nUse these defaults directly. Do not read a separate role playbook.\n\n- Product: launch plan, roadmap note, competitor positioning, PRD outline, exec update. Context: Drive/Notion, Slack, Linear/GitHub, Calendar.\n- Engineering: bug investigation, PR summary, failing tests or CI, local changes, implementation planning, code-change docs. Context: Drive, Slack, Gmail, existing folder.\n- Sales: follow-up email, account brief, customer summary, discovery questions, objection handling. Context: Gmail, Drive/Notion, Slack, Calendar.\n- Design: feedback-to-tasks, critique summary, design handoff, flow comparison, prototype brief. Context: Figma, Slack, Drive/Notion, existing folder.\n- Data science: dataset analysis, experiment summary, metrics readout, dashboard plan, methodology notes. Context: Drive/Sheets, Slack, Gmail, Calendar.\n- Finance: budget summary, forecast model, finance brief, spreadsheet analysis, review questions. Context: Drive/Sheets, Gmail, Slack, existing folder.\n- Student: study guide, assignment plan, outline, practice quiz. Context: existing folder, Drive, Calendar, Gmail.\n\nFor Engineering, prefer broad engineering workflows over narrow signal sources such as a single log, digest, or channel.\n\n## Step 2 - Task\n\nSay:\n\n\u003e Got it. Let's set Codex up around real {role_or_roles} work.\n\u003e\n\u003e What's something we can try knocking off your list today?\n\nThen call `setup_codex_step` with `step: \"task\"`. Use connectors, folders, and local files as context sources.\n\nSay:\n\n\u003e Great. A good {artifact_or_task} usually pulls from a few places: {source_examples}.\n\u003e\n\u003e I can pull that context from your existing tools. Where should we look first?\n\nThen call `setup_codex_step` with `step: \"context\"`. Do not list source options in prose.\n\nDo not assume every connected source is relevant. A repo, folder, inbox, Drive, Slack workspace, or channel is only a place to look. If only containers are known, run candidate discovery and ask for a concrete anchor if needed.\n\n## Step 3.75 - Substance Pass\n\nBefore creating the artifact, do a substance pass over retrieved context. Extract concrete entities the artifact depends on: projects, workstreams, owners, dates, decisions, metrics, blockers, artifacts, customers, files, PRs, risks, open questions, or next actions.\n\nIf the first artifact would mostly say that important substance is missing, do not write it yet. Ask targeted follow-up questions to fill the most important gaps. Use `request_onboarding_input` when the answer can be offered as 2-3 concrete options. Ask plain text only when the missing input cannot be reasonably optioned.\n\nFor review, planning, brief, status, readiness, or operating-review artifacts, include a concrete status table, decision list, or workstream list when possible. Each row should be grounded in retrieved context or clearly marked as unknown. Do not stop at generic questions and next steps unless the user explicitly asks for a lightweight starter.\n\nGap-fill questions do not count as the two output-direction refinement questions. Keep them focused on missing substance, such as owner, status, scope, milestone, decision, evidence, metric, risk, or next action.\n\n## Step 4 - Refine Intent\n\nAsk only questions that shape the first artifact. Use `request_onboarding_input` with 2-3 concrete options and one recommended default.\n\nAfter the substance pass and any needed gap-fill questions, ask at least two preference or tradeoff questions unless the user already supplied the criteria.\n\nLocator questions, candidate-selection questions, source-selection questions, authorization prompts, recovery questions, and substance gap-fill questions do not count toward the two required output-direction refinements.\n\nGood refinement dimensions include artifact shape, focus, audience, depth, tone, scope, constraints, or next action.\n\nFor engineering and debugging, useful refinements include:\n\n- `What kind of debugging should we start with?`: `Reproduce a bug (Recommended)`, `Investigate logs or errors`, `Fix failing tests or CI`\n- `Where is the issue showing up?`: `Local workspace (Recommended)`, `GitHub or CI`, `Production or logs`\n- `What should the first artifact be?`: `Root-cause summary (Recommended)`, `Fix plan`, `Patch or PR`\n\nFor code review, ask `What kind of code review should we start with?` before asking for a URL or diff:\n\n- `Open PR (Recommended)`: Review a GitHub PR by URL\n- `Local changes`: Review the current workspace diff\n- `Paste diff`: Review a diff pasted into chat\n\nSummarize the answers in one concise sentence, then mark `Give Codex context` complete.\n\n## Step 5 - Create Artifact\n\nCreate something real from the selected task, retrieved context, task anchor, and refinements. Use the lightest existing artifact surface that fits:\n\n- Document for briefs, plans, memos, PRDs, policies, proposals, and longer writeups\n- Spreadsheet for trackers, budgets, scoring, inventories, or analysis tables\n- Deck for readouts, launches, exec reviews, or customer-facing narratives\n- GitHub for code changes, issues, and pull requests\n- Site or app only for explicit web or app prototypes\n- Chat only for short copy, summaries, or when no external artifact surface is available\n\nAvoid in-thread drafts when a real artifact surface fits better. Use the appropriate connector or artifact tool to create the deliverable.\n\nBefore creating anything, apply the context-recovery, task-anchor, substance-pass, gap-fill, and refinement rules.\n\nAfter creating the artifact or allowed starter template, call `setup_codex_step` with `step: \"complete\"` exactly once.\n\nClose with one sentence naming and linking the artifact and one sentence inviting 6.4 CI, Semaphore, artefactos y GO\\\\n\\\\nSchema CI obligatorio: repo/rama/candidate SHA/provider/proyecto/run/pipeline/attempt, jobs/checks requeridos, estado/conclusión, timestamps y fuente observable. Rechazar rc no cero aunque haya JSON; SHA ausente/distinto, colección vacía, UNKNOWN, skipped/cancelled, intento viejo y jobs parciales no son SUCCESS. Consultar todos los checks obligatorios, paginación y política de proveedor configurada.\\\\n\\\\nSemaphore: obtener identidad y resultado del pipeline/job concreto, no body global ni eco de args. Recoger failed_jobs con block/job/step/exit/log y origen; manejar SHA abreviado con resolución canónica demostrable, no substring. Auth legítima puede requerir acceso humano, sin bypass. Reproducción local solo con checkout exacto y aislamiento de credenciales/servicios; una allowlist textual `pytest` no limita lo que ejecuta el test. Distinguir `COLLECTION_COMPLETE`, `REPRODUCED`, `VALIDATION_PASSED` y `NOT_REPRODUCIBLE`; reportar por qué una reproducción no aplica, sin inventar PASS de tests.\\\\n\\\\nReplan: corregir regex corrupto y probar enlaces `.md`, blob/data/download y forma de enlace ofrecida por Chat. Si falta artefacto pedir corrección una vez por mensaje y continuar al nuevo; nunca fabricar bytes desde la paráfrasis del LLM.\\\\n\\\\nGO exige evento del turno correcto después de revisión final, repo/rama/candidato atribuibles, HEAD antes/después de consulta CI coincidente, CI exacto vigente, obligaciones/acciones/outbox completas y despliegue verificado si lo requiere la tarea. The BiGRU is an enhanced\\n[L206] type of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) that combines the advan-\\n[L207] tages of bidirectional processing and gating mechanisms, excelling\\n[L208] in sequence modeling tasks.\\n\\n[L210] The BiGRU network consists of two independent GRU layers:\\n[L211] a forward GRU layer and a backward GRU layer. These two GRU\\n[L212] layers process the input sequence in both forward and backward\\n[L213] directions, enabling the network to leverage both past and future\\n[L214] information for predictions[8]. The GRU unit controls the flow of in-\\n[L215] formation through the introduction of update gates and reset gates,\\n[L216] effectively addressing the vanishing/exploding gradient problem.\\n\\n[L218] The basic equations for the GRU unit are as follows:\\n[L219] Let 𝑥𝑡 be the input at time step 𝑡 , ℎ𝑡−1 be the hidden state at\\n\\n[L221] time step 𝑡 − 1, 𝑧𝑡 be the update gate, 𝑟𝑡 be the reset gate, ℎ̃𝑡 be the\\n[L222] candidate hidden state, and ℎ𝑡 be the hidden state at time step 𝑡 .\\nThen,\\n\\n[L225] 𝑧𝑡 = 𝜎 (𝑊𝑧𝑥𝑡 +𝑈𝑧ℎ𝑡−1 + 𝑏𝑧) (1)\\n[L226] 𝑟𝑡 = 𝜎 (𝑊𝑟𝑥𝑡 +𝑈𝑟ℎ𝑡−1 + 𝑏𝑟 ) (2)\\n\\n[L228] ℎ̃𝑡 = tanh(𝑊ℎ𝑥𝑡 +𝑈ℎ (𝑟𝑡 ◦ ℎ𝑡−1) + 𝑏ℎ) (3)\\n\\n[L230] ℎ𝑡 = (1 − 𝑧𝑡 ) ◦ ℎ̃𝑡 + 𝑧𝑡 ◦ ℎ𝑡−1 (4)\\n\\n[L232] where 𝜎 denotes the sigmoid activation function, tanh denotes\\n[L233] the hyperbolic tangent activation function, and ◦ represents element-\\n[L234] wise multiplication.\\n\\n[L236] In the BiGRU, we compute both the forward and backward states\\n[L237] of the GRU:\\n\\n−→\\n[L240] ℎ𝑡 = GRU(−→𝑥𝑡 ,\\n\\n−−−→\\n[L243] ℎ𝑡−1) (5)\\n\\n←−\\n[L246] ℎ𝑡 = GRU(←−𝑥𝑡 ,\\n\\n←−−−\\n[L249] ℎ𝑡+1) (6)\\n\\nwhere\\n−→\\n[L253] ℎ𝑡 represents the forward GRU state at time step 𝑡 , and\\n\\n←−\\nℎ𝑡\\n\\n[L258] represents the backward GRU state at time step 𝑡 . The final hidden\\n[L259] state ℎ𝑡 can be obtained by combining these two directional states,\\n[L260] such as concatenation or weighted sum.\\n\\n[L262] The BiGRU network is capable of capturing long-term depen-\\n[L263] dencies in sequences more effectively and, due to its consideration\\n[L264] of both past and future context, it demonstrates higher accuracy in\\n[L265] time series prediction tasks. By training the BiGRU network, we\\n[L266] can forecast future closing prices of IBM’s stock, providing valuable\\n[L267] insights for investors.\\n\\n[L269] 2.2 TCN\\n[L270] In this study, we use IBM’s stock closing price dataset and apply\\n[L271] the Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) for feature extraction,\\n[L272] which subsequently aids in time series prediction. But the stock market is volatile and unstable,\\n[L123] which often leaves investors confused and helpless. The basic analysis method is the\\n[L127] comprehensive data, economics, securities and other knowledge,\\n[L128] through their own experience of the stock market judgment and\\n[L129] analysis methods [2-3]. Combining the two and\\n[L142] applying them together in stock forecasting, such forecasting not\\n[L143] only simulates the subjective judgment of people when buying\\n[L144] stocks, but also explores the law from the data, thus improving\\n[L145] the accuracy of stock forecasting, avoiding investors’ risks, and\\n[L146] guaranteeing considerable returns.\\n\\n[L148] This article uses domestic Shanghai and Shenzhen A-share data\\n[L149] as an example to construct a combined model of ARIMA time series\\n[L150] [5] model and BP neural network through Python, and integrates\\n[L151] it with the emotional tendency value of financial news text infor-\\n[L152] mation.
